gaps.title: Fallback authentication bypasses active SSO enforcement
gaps.jtbd: When the external LMS fails, I want the system to permit fallback authentication, so that users can still log in without bypassing SSO security during normal operations.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given the external Moodle LMS is operational, When a user attempts to log in with an invalid SSO token but a correct fallback password, Then the system should reject the login and enforce SSO.
gaps.reason: The brief specifies 'автономный fallback' for LMS failures. A domain-standard implementation must restrict local fallback exclusively to genuine upstream LMS outages (e.g., server errors or timeouts). Currently, the system falls back to the local password check simply if the provided token is invalid, allowing users to intentionally bypass centralized SSO policies at any time.

gaps.title: Missing automatic Moodle context binding for new strains
gaps.jtbd: When I register a new closed strain, I want the system to automatically bind it to my Moodle department and courses, so that access is intrinsically segregated without manual data entry.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given an authenticated Moodle user, When they create a new strain, Then the system should automatically assign the strain's access department and course based on the user's current Moodle profile, ignoring arbitrary client-provided access parameters.
gaps.reason: The brief requires 'Автоматическое разграничение прав доступа... на основе кафедр и курсов Moodle'. While analytical reports automatically inherit the creator's Moodle context, the StrainController blindly trusts client-provided access strings during creation, failing to automatically enforce the user's Moodle departmental boundary on new strains.
